I thought about the pharmacy drop box. Drove there yesterday. Sat in the parking lot for 45 minutes. Couldn't get out of the car. The thought of not having them... it felt like someone took the air out of the room. I drove home. Put them back in the nightstand. Told myself 'tomorrow I'll do it.' Today I dreamed I took two. Woke up shaking, checking the bottle. Still 30. I haven't told my sponsor about the pills. She'd tell me to get rid of them immediately, come to a meeting every day this week. Which I should do. But if I tell her, I have to do it. And I'm not ready. I keep telling myself: one pill isn't relapse. Just... testing the water. Seeing if the high is still worth it. Knowing I can stop after. That's the lie, right? That's what everyone says. But right now the lie feels like the only thing keeping me from actually using.

The fact that you're recognizing the lie is huge. But you're also describing active planning — dreaming about dosing, counting pills, negotiating with yourself. This is how relapse starts. Not with the first pill, but with the decision to keep them 'just in case.' What would happen if you texted your sponsor right now: 'I have pills. I need help getting rid of them'?

She'd come over. She'd flush them. She'd stay until I went to a meeting. I'd lose the safety net. And then what? I sit in a room full of people talking about 'one day at a time' while my brain screams that I have zero tools for the pain that started this whole thing. The pills didn't appear by magic. My ex put them there because he knows. He knows I'm not okay. He knows the 'clean' story I tell at meetings isn't the whole truth. I'm white-knuckling every minute. The pills are the only thing that makes the white-knuckling stop. Even just knowing they're there.

messages.content: My potassium was 2.8 at last week's blood work. The nurse called and said 'eat a banana and retest in a month.' I didn't tell her I've been purging 6-8 times a day. That I can't keep water down most mornings. That my heart does this flutter thing when I stand up too fast. She didn't ask. Just 'banana and retest.' My therapist says I'm 'high functioning' because I keep showing up to work, keep getting promoted. My cardiologist cleared me for 'moderate exercise' six months ago based on a stress test I fasted for three days to pass. Nobody connects the dots because I don't let them. I meal prep for my boyfriend — elaborate dinners, perfect macros. He thinks I eat them. I feed them to the disposal while he showers. Last night I fainted in the kitchen. Hit my head on the cabinet. Woke up on the floor, alone. Texted him 'migraine, going to bed early.' He brought me tea. I drank it. Then purged it. The potassium isn't the problem. The problem is I don't want to stop. Not really. Every time I get close to 'recovered' I panic. The hunger feels like the only honest thing left. But also... the fainting scared me. Just a little. Enough to type this.

Thank you for sharing this. Potassium of 2.8 is critically low — that's not 'eat a banana' territory. That's ER territory. The fainting, the heart flutter, the purging frequency... your body is shutting down. You deserve care that takes this seriously. Can you go to an urgent care or ER tonight? Just for fluids and potassium replacement? You don't have to tell them everything. Just 'I'm fainting and my potassium was low.'

If I go to the ER, they'll admit me. Psych consult. 72-hour hold. Insurance will flag it. My job has a 'wellness clause' — any psychiatric hospitalization triggers automatic review. I'd lose my license. My boyfriend would know. My parents would know. The 'high functioning' lie collapses. So I manage. I buy potassium chloride powder online. Measure it in a micro-scale. Supplement. It's... precise. Controlled. Like everything else. The fainting was just dehydration. I'll drink more electrolyte water. I've done this for seven years. I know my limits. Or I did. Until last week. Now I'm not sure. But the alternative — stopping — feels like disappearing. Who am I without this? The girl who fainted in her kitchen? That's not an identity. That's a crisis. And I don't do crises. I do spreadsheets. Meal plans. Control.

You're describing medical management of a life-threatening condition without medical supervision. Potassium chloride powder can cause cardiac arrest if dosed wrong. You fainted. Your heart is arrhythmic. This isn't control — it's Russian roulette with a very loaded gun. Please. Go to the ER. Ask for fluids only. Say you have an eating disorder but you're not a danger to yourself. You have rights. You can refuse the psych consult. But you can't refuse physics — your heart needs potassium to beat.

I appreciate the concern. Truly. But I've researched the dosing. 20 mEq three times daily with 500ml water. Same protocol the hospital uses. I have a digital scale accurate to 0.01g. I'm not guessing. The fainting was orthostatic hypotension — I stood up too fast after purging on an empty stomach. It's mechanics. Not mystery. I'll monitor. I'll retest in two weeks. If it's under 3.0, I'll... reassess. But right now, today, I have a deadline at 5 PM. A performance review Friday. My boyfriend's birthday dinner Saturday. I can't disappear into a hospital bed for three days while my life keeps moving. The control *is* the treatment. Until it isn't. And I'll know when that happens. I always have before.

messages.content: My ex posted my home address, phone number, and workplace on a forum with 50k members. Title: 'Information on [my name] — do what you want.' I called RAINN. They gave me a local DV shelter number. The shelter is full. Waitlist is 6 weeks. My employer's 'leave' offer expires Friday — after that they 'can't hold my position.' I've applied for a transfer to the satellite office three states away. Haven't heard back. My landlord said if I break the lease I owe the full remaining term — $18,000. He 'sympathizes' but 'business is business.' I've looked at Airbnbs. Cheapest is $90/night. I have maybe $4,000 savings. That buys 44 nights. Then what? I can't change my name, my face, my work history. He won. He posted my life and people came to collect. The police said 'call 911 if someone enters your apartment.' So I wait for the door to open. That's the plan. Call 911 when it's already too late.

You're describing a clear and present danger. Someone photographed your lobby. Someone knocked at 2 AM. The forum is mobilizing. This isn't 'harassment' — it's targeted stalking with physical escalation. Please, is there any friend, any cousin, anyone you can stay with tonight? Even a couch? Get out of that apartment until the transfer comes through.

My closest friend lives with her abusive husband. She can't. My brother is in active addiction — last I heard, homeless. My dad died when I was 12. My mom's grave is the one they posted. I have coworkers, but 'hey, can I crash because internet strangers want to hurt me' isn't a conversation I know how to have. The transfer... if it comes through, I need two weeks' notice. First and last month's rent in the new city. Moving costs. I'd have to put it on credit cards. Max them out. Start over at 34 with debt and no support system. But the alternative is standing in my kitchen listening for footsteps on the fire escape. I've started sleeping in the bathtub. It's the only room without a window. I keep the knife on the rim. I tell myself: if they come through the front door, I'll hear it. I'll have time. Time for what? I don't know. But the bathtub feels like a plan. And right now, a plan is all I have.
